papers.title: Finite Element Simulation of the Temperature Field and Residual Stress in GH536 Superalloy Treated by Selective Laser Melting

llm.relevance_to_user: 与用户研究方向无关，该论文涉及镍基高温合金的选择性激光熔化温度场和残余应力模拟，未包含生物医学植入物、多孔结构或力学性能验证。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve biomedical implants, porous structures, stress shielding, mechanical testing (fatigue), surface roughness, or osseointegration; it focuses on thermal and residual stress simulation of a nickel-based superalloy for non-biomedical applications.

summary_zh.motivation: 模拟GH536合金SLM过程中的温度场和残余应力分布。
summary_zh.method: 采用有限元方法对选择性激光熔化过程进行热-力耦合模拟。
summary_zh.result: 获得了温度场和残余应力的分布规律。
summary_zh.validation: 数值模拟结果未经实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To simulate the temperature field and residual stress distribution during selective laser melting of GH536 superalloy.
summary_en.method: A coupled thermal-mechanical finite element model was developed for the SLM process.
summary_en.result: The temperature field and residual stress distribution were obtained and analyzed.
summary_en.validation: The simulation results were not validated by experiments.

papers.venue: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons

llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on clinical management of periprosthetic joint infection, with no biomechanical modeling, stress shielding quantification, implant stability analysis, or finite element simulation.

summary_zh.motivation: 探讨全髋关节置换术后假体周围感染的一期翻修管理策略
summary_zh.method: 综述当前一期交换手术的适应症、技术要点及临床证据
summary_zh.result: 一期翻修在选择性病例中可有效控制感染并改善功能
summary_zh.validation: 基于临床病例系列和回顾性研究结果

summary_en.motivation: To review the management strategies for periprosthetic joint infection after total hip arthroplasty, focusing on one-stage exchange.
summary_en.method: A narrative review of indications, surgical techniques, and clinical outcomes of one-stage exchange arthroplasty.
summary_en.result: One-stage exchange is effective in selected patients for infection control and functional improvement.
summary_en.validation: Clinical evidence from retrospective case series and cohort studies.

papers.title: Biomechanical properties of 3D-printed bone scaffolds are improved by treatment with CRFP.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: One of the major challenges in orthopedics is to develop implants that overcome current postoperative problems such as osteointegration, proper load bearing, and stress shielding. Current implant techniques such as allografts or endoprostheses never reach full bone integration, and the risk of fracture due to stress shielding is a major concern. To overcome this, a novel technique of reverse engineering to create artificial scaffolds was designed and tested. The purpose of the study is to create a new generation of implants that are both biocompatible and biomimetic. METHODS: 3D-printed scaffolds based on physiological trabecular bone patterning were printed. MC3T3 cells were cultured on these scaffolds in osteogenic media, with and without the addition of Calcitonin Receptor Fragment Peptide (CRFP) in order to assess bone formation on the surfaces of the scaffolds. Integrity of these cell-seeded bone-coated scaffolds was tested for their mechanical strength. RESULTS: The results show that cellular proliferation and bone matrix formation are both supported by our 3D-printed scaffolds. The mechanical strength of the scaffolds was enhanced by trabecular patterning in the order of 20% for compression strength and 60% for compressive modulus. Furthermore, cell-seeded trabecular scaffolds modulus increased fourfold when treated with CRFP. CONCLUSION: Upon mineralization, the cell-seeded trabecular implants treated with osteo-inductive agents and pretreated with CRFP showed a significant increase in the compressive modulus. This work will lead to creating 3D structures that can be used in the replacement of not only bone segments, but entire bones.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注骨支架的3D打印和生物力学性能，不涉及髋关节假体或股骨柄的应力遮挡或微动分析。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not quantify femoral stem stress shielding, micromotion, or bone-implant interface mechanics; it focuses on scaffold biocompatibility and compressive strength, not hip implant design or FEA.

summary_zh.motivation: 改善骨植入物的骨整合和力学性能。
summary_zh.method: 3D打印骨小梁支架并用CRFP处理，检测细胞增殖和力学强度。
summary_zh.result: CRFP处理使细胞种植支架的压缩模量提高四倍。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞培养和压缩力学测试。

summary_en.motivation: To develop biocompatible and biomimetic 3D-printed bone scaffolds that improve osseointegration and reduce stress shielding.
summary_en.method: Scaffolds were 3D-printed with trabecular patterns, seeded with MC3T3 cells, cultured with or without CRFP, and tested for compressive mechanical properties.
summary_en.result: CRFP treatment increased the compressive modulus of cell-seeded trabecular scaffolds fourfold compared to untreated controls.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed via in vitro cell culture assays and uniaxial compression mechanical testing.
